subject: Escalation: Dawn-scale p95/p99 latency surge impacting FinPulse
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@finpulse.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 spikes this morning during autoscale (morning batch)

Irene —

We started seeing a large and reproducible latency spike in the morning batch window starting ~08:30 PST. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s, p99 to ~4.2s for our hosted API calls. This coincided with an autoscale event (several GPU nodes added). The pattern repeats across two separate deployments. Our users experienced timeouts in critical flows.

Attached: p99_plot_20260718.png (tokenized p95/p99 plot), logs_tail.txt (sample tails). We need immediate mitigation and an explanation — this is affecting our SLAs.

Can you confirm whether you saw warm-pool activity or any provision delays?

- Julia
Principal SRE, FinPulse


From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Severe p99 spikes this morning during autoscale (FinPulse) — needs triage and exec note

Forwarding FinPulse escalation. TL;DR: p95/p99 regressions during a GPU autoscale window. Customer attached plots and tails.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether new instances were cold (no pre-warmed cache / model jyit) and if any node boot-time throttling occurred?
- SRE: capture sampling traces and top-ops across the window (attach trace_sampling.zip).
- PM/CS (Marissa): we will likely need to offer a service credit and an interim mitigation plan for the customer.

I will keep Julia updated — please treat as severity-high.

Thanks,
Irene
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:01:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe p99 spikes this morning during autoscale (FinPulse) — triage notes

On Sat, Jul 18, 2026 at 9:34 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding FinPulse escalation.

Quick triage from infra: we see a correlated spike in pod init latencies during the 08:20–08:45 window. Root cause looks like a combination of:
- New GPU instances coming up without warmed KV-cache (model context cold).
- Kernel-level nvlink handshake delays on a subset of A100 hosts (~2 of 12 in the pool) which pushed per-token scheduling into slower fallback paths.

Immediate mitigation I pushed (10:48):
- Temporarily increased min-warm-pool to 2 for the FinPulse pool to keep a small cohort always warm.
- Enabled aggressive prefix-cache reuse for their tenant for the next 24h.

Longer term actions:
- SRE to add a pre-warm runbook that synthesizes a short keep-alive workload during scale events.
- Release a kernel telemetry patch to detect nvlink handshakes failing and auto-fallback earlier.

I'll attach the sampled traces (trace_sampling.zip) and a short note for execs. If we need a rollback option, we can pin them to a smaller reserved pool.

— Aditya
Lead Infra Engineer

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 12:26:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe p99 spikes this morning during autoscale (FinPulse) — SRE follow-up

Adding SRE notes:
- Confirmed that 2 hosts showed nvlink handshake anomalies; they were serviced and removed from rotation at 11:05. Logs attached in logs_tail.txt.
- The autoscaler launched 5 instances; three reached ready state with full model load, two entered degraded mode and relied on CPU fallback paths for the first ~90s, which explains the tail.
- We think root cause is transient host-level firmware combo + a race in our model load path that doesn't re-try fast enough when nvlink fails.

Customer-facing next steps I propose:
1) Short-term: apologize, summarize mitigation (min-warm-pool + removal of two hosts) and offer an SLA credit for the incident window.
2) Mid-term (1–2 weeks): rollout pre-warm on scale events + increase default warm pool for large accounts during morning window.
3) Engineering fix (3–4 weeks): add robust handshake detection + faster model load retry with warmed cache seeding.

Marissa — please confirm the credit band and whether we need Exec visibility.

- Dylan
Senior SRE, Serving Infrastructure

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation summary and exec note (FinPulse morning-scale p99)

Thanks team — good triage. Summary for execs and FinPulse:
- Incident window: 2026-07-18 08:20–08:45 PST.
- Impact: FinPulse p95/p99 spikes (p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~4.2s) during autoscale. Root cause: two GPU hosts with nvlink handshake failures leading to slow fallback paths and cold model loads.
- Actions taken: removed bad hosts, increased warm-pool to 2, enabled aggressive prefix reuse, captured traces and logs (attached).
- Customer ask: formal RCA and a goodwill credit.

Requested approvals:
- Approve issuing a one-month usage credit (up to $8k cap) as a good-faith gesture while we complete fixes.
- Approve priority engineering work to ship pre-warm and handshake detection in next sprint.

If approved, I will send a customer-facing note with a short timeline (RCA in 3 business days, fixes staged in 2–4 weeks).

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
